title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
summary: JSSA replaces full-KV attention during long-context decoding with training-free token-level sparse selection scored in a learned shared low-dimensional query-key subspace, executed via a gather-free indexed-attention kernel compatible with the standard GQA KV-cache layout. The cost is integrating a custom kernel and computing the subspace projection per model, plus residual selection overhead; the subspace is derived from a closed-form spectral solution, so there is no training pipeline to maintain. It can fail if the low-dimensional scoring loses ranking structure on out-of-distribution workloads, if the kernel is unavailable or unoptimized for the reader's hardware (gains were demonstrated on a B200, not a 24 GB consumer GPU), or if competing sparse methods' generation-length inflation reappears on atypical prompts.
rationale: The method is training-free and directly reduces decoding-time KV-cache traffic, which suits constrained infrastructure, but the reported gains depend on a custom kernel validated on B200-class hardware and must be confirmed on the reader's specific GPU and workload before production adoption.

claims.statement: JSSA replaces full-KV attention during long-context decoding with training-free token-level sparse selection scored in a learned shared low-dimensional query-key subspace, executed via a gather-free indexed-attention kernel compatible with the standard GQA KV-cache layout. The cost is integrating a custom kernel and computing the subspace projection per model, plus residual selection overhead; the subspace is derived from a closed-form spectral solution, so there is no training pipeline to maintain. It can fail if the low-dimensional scoring loses ranking structure on out-of-distribution workloads, if the kernel is unavailable or unoptimized for the reader's hardware (gains were demonstrated on a B200, not a 24 GB consumer GPU), or if competing sparse methods' generation-length inflation reappears on atypical prompts.

Up to 6.43x decoding throughput versus full-KV attention at 128K context on an NVIDIA B200, while remaining close to full-KV accuracy and reaching 96-99% of model-native DSA throughput without training.
